steps.name: Sample structure QC on liver treated vs control counts
steps.question: Do the 3 treated and 3 control liver samples separate by condition on a blind variance-stabilized PCA, and are there outlier samples or library-size issues before any DE test is run?

acceptance_criteria: vst(blind=TRUE) computed on the raw count matrix (12000 genes x 6 samples, after dropping the gene-symbol column)
PCA plot on the top 500 most variable genes colored by condition (treated/control)
Sample-to-sample Euclidean distance heatmap produced
Library size (total counts) per sample reported and compared across the two groups
Any sample that does not cluster with its labeled condition or has markedly divergent library size is flagged explicitly in the output, not silently dropped

steps.name: Pre-filter low-count genes
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes have enough counts to be tested for differential expression between treated and control liver samples, given only 3 replicates per group?

grounding.reason: With n=3 per group and raw counts, the minimal pre-filter of >=10 counts in >=3 samples is grounded; independent filtering later does the rest, so the pre-filter is deliberately not stricter.

acceptance_criteria: Filter keeps a gene only if it has >=10 raw counts in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size)
Number of genes retained after filtering is reported

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
steps.question: Which of the filtered genes are differentially expressed between drug-treated and control liver samples (3 vs 3), using DESeq2's median-of-ratios normalization and Wald test with an explicit control reference level?

grounding.reason: R-0017 flags that at n=3/group the test has low power (finds a minority of true DE genes, mostly large-effect); alpha is kept at its default (0.05) rather than loosened, and the outcome is reported with the power caveat rather than overclaimed, per the flag's instruction.

acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 dataset built with design ~condition, with condition releveled so 'control' is the explicit reference level
Median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside DESeq2 (no separate normalization of counts before the model)
Wald test run for the contrast condition treated vs control

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test: treated vs control (robustness cross-check)
steps.question: Do the genes called differentially expressed by DESeq2 replicate under edgeR's quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts and design, and what is the overlap between the two methods' significant gene sets?

grounding.reason: At n=3/group, DESeq2 Wald and edgeR quasi-likelihood are the two recommended tools; running both and reporting the overlap as the high-confidence set is the grounded robustness practice (R-0042), consistent with Schurch et al. 2016 (PMID 27022035) finding both control FDR at low replicate numbers.

acceptance_criteria: edgeR DGEList built from the same filtered count matrix and design (~condition, control as reference)
TMM normalization factors estimated, dispersion estimated with estimateDisp, glmQLFit + glmQLFTest run for the treated-vs-control contrast

Intersection and each method's unique significant gene set reported; the intersection is labeled the high-confidence set and the union is not presented as the result

steps.name: Shrink log2 fold changes with apeglm
steps.question: What is the apeglm-shrunken, noise-corrected effect size for the treated-vs-control contrast for each tested gene, to use for ranking and plotting instead of the noisy raw estimate?

acceptance_criteria: lfcShrink run with type='apeglm' on the treated-vs-control coefficient from the DESeq2 fit

steps.name: Multiple testing correction and DE gene table
steps.question: Which genes pass a Benjamini-Hochberg-adjusted p-value threshold of 0.05 for the treated-vs-control liver contrast, after DESeq2's independent filtering?

grounding.reason: BH at alpha=0.05 with independent filtering is the grounded default; the p-value histogram diagnostic is required before the adjusted p-values are trusted, especially important to check given the small n=3 design.

acceptance_criteria: p-value histogram (unadjusted) plotted and its shape (flat/left-skewed vs anomalous) reported before trusting the BH adjustment
results() called with independent filtering on and alpha=0.05 matching the reporting cutoff

Count of genes tested after filtering, count of genes with padj < 0.05, and count of NA-adjusted genes (split by independent-filtering NA vs Cook's-outlier NA) all reported

plan.title: Liver drug vs control DE (n=3/3) + pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12,000-gene, 7-sample bulk RNA-seq counts from Salmon on human liver tissue, comparing 3 drug-treated vs 3 control samples in a single unpaired batch (metadata: 6 samples with condition; note the counts file has 7 columns for 6 samples plus the gene symbol column). Given raw integer counts and n=3 per group, the grounded procedure (Inflexa knowledge service) is: blind-VST sample-structure QC before any test, a minimal count pre-filter, DESeq2's built-in median-of-ratios normalization, an explicit reference-level model (control as reference), a DESeq2 Wald test with edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test run in parallel for a robustness overlap (both are the recommended tools at n=3, per Schurch et al. 2016, RNA, PMID 27022035), apeglm shrinkage of the reported fold change, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control with independent filtering, and fgsea preranked GSEA (ranked on the DESeq2 Wald statistic per the knowledge service's disputed-rule resolution) against MSigDB Hallmark followed by Reactome and WikiPathways as the human-appropriate collection order — all gene-set files are staged locally (MSigDB Hallmark, Reactome, WikiPathways human GMTs). Because n=3 per group is explicitly flagged as low-power by the knowledge service (R-0017, R-0094: only 20-40% of true DE genes recovered at n=3 unless fold change exceeds ~4-fold, per Schurch 2016), the report step states this expected-power ceiling explicitly rather than treating an absent gene as evidence of no change, and the significance threshold is not loosened to compensate. An over-representation (hypergeometric) enrichment test is deliberately excluded per the knowledge service's rejection of that method for this design (few significant genes expected at n=3 gives ORA no power) — fgsea's full-ranked-list approach is used instead, which is robust to a short significant-gene list.
